caption:
The note ban was meant to trap black money. Then 99.3% of it walked back into the banks.

₹15.41 lakh crore of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes were banned in November 2016. By the RBI's own count, ₹15.31 lakh crore came back.

So where did the black money go? Watch it twice.

Source: RBI Annual Report 2017-18

24.67 lakh bank accounts in India were flagged as "mules", used to move scam money so it can't be traced.

The government's cyber crime centre (I4C) says its suspect registry has helped block ₹8,031.56 crore. Many mules are ordinary people who "rent out" an account for a small cut, and end up holding the case.

Source: Lok Sabha reply, Dec 2025

caption:
₹36,793 crore. Money linked to India sitting in Swiss banks at the end of 2025.

The total (CHF 3.25 billion) fell 8%, but customer deposits jumped more than 50% to CHF 524 million. The twist: Swiss authorities say these numbers "cannot be considered as black money". Most of it is banks and companies.

So who's hiding what? You decide.

Source: Swiss National Bank annual data, released 19 Jun 2026
